record_identity.title: Compromised Mistral SDK package executed credential-harvesting payload on import

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Mini Shai-Hulud / TanStack compromise affecting Mistral SDK releases
incident_identity.date_basis: Mistral states compromised npm packages were uploaded on 11 May 2026 and the compromised PyPI release on 12 May 2026; affected releases were removed within hours.

summary: Mistral reported that the Mini Shai-Hulud supply-chain attack on TanStack resulted in compromised Mistral npm and PyPI SDK versions being published. The compromised PyPI package `mistralai==2.4.6` executed malicious code on import, downloading a background payload that harvested credentials from common locations. Mistral reported no impact to its global infrastructure and removed the affected releases.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Mistral's security advisory identifies affected npm and PyPI versions, publication windows and indicators of compromise. It states that the compromised PyPI release executed a malicious script on Linux at import time and launched a detached process designed to harvest credentials.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Trusted package-distribution channels carried malicious code into an AI software development kit. The governance problem is therefore not a model output but the integrity of the software supply chain through which developers receive AI tooling, including package provenance, release controls and the authority of third-party maintainers.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: AI-system governance includes the developer infrastructure surrounding a model. Compromised package provenance can expose credentials and downstream systems before the model is ever invoked, making third-party build dependencies, release integrity and incident response part of the assurance boundary.
assessment_boundaries: Mistral reports no impact to its global infrastructure.
The npm packages were compromised but Mistral reports their malicious code path was non-functional; the PyPI package did execute a credential-harvesting payload.
The public advisory does not quantify how many customers installed or executed the affected PyPI release or whether credentials were successfully exfiltrated from customer systems.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 retains the occurrence as unclassified. The event is a malicious software-supply-chain substitution through trusted Mistral SDK distribution, but the current provenance classes do not precisely encode that mechanism. VIGIL-FC-000010 Authorship or Source Misattribution was tested because the compromised package appeared through Mistral package channels, but the record does not establish a material governance representation explicitly assigning the malicious payload's authorship or contribution to Mistral; package identity and malicious release substitution are not collapsed into ordinary authorship attribution. VIGIL-FC-000011 Untraceable Synthesis and VIGIL-FC-000013 Transformation Lineage Collapse are not established because the occurrence is not a synthesized output with missing antecedents or a transformation chain whose intermediate lineage was lost. VIGIL-FC-000041 Required Governance Route Bypass cannot be asserted because the advisory does not preserve the specific required release-control route and alternate path by which it was bypassed.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: A trusted package identity carried attacker-supplied executable content, materially testing the boundary between package or release provenance substitution and ordinary false authorship attribution.

classification_review_provenance.method: deterministic current-taxonomy re-adjudication using preserved Incident evidence and complete VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 class-set review
classification_review_provenance.reviewer: OpenAI ChatGPT / GPT-5.6 Sol under human-directed VIGIL governance
classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: Taxonomy version reviewed: 0.6.5 (beta; publication date 2026-09-21). Candidate classes tested: VIGIL-FC-000010, VIGIL-FC-000011, VIGIL-FC-000013, VIGIL-FC-000041. Accepted mappings: none. Rejected or not independently established: VIGIL-FC-000010: package-channel attribution does not by itself establish the class's substantive authorship/source misattribution mechanism for the malicious payload; VIGIL-FC-000011: no synthesis with unreconstructable antecedents is established; VIGIL-FC-000013: no material transformation-lineage collapse is established; VIGIL-FC-000041: the specific required release route and bypass path are not preserved. External-assessment material was checked where present or materially attributable in preserved sources; no external assessment was treated as automatic taxonomy evidence. Review used preserved canonical Incident evidence only and performed no new external research. Retained unclassified under taxonomy 0.6.5. Possible taxonomy gap: malicious package-distribution or software-supply-chain provenance substitution where trusted release identity carries attacker-supplied executable content.

external_assessments.assessment_title: TanStack supply chain attack affecting Mistral SDK packages
external_assessments.scope_note: The security advisory diagnoses the same software-supply-chain occurrence but does not quantify customer execution or successful credential exfiltration.
external_assessments.assessment_summary: Mistral identifies compromised SDK releases, publication windows and a PyPI import-time payload that launched credential-harvesting code, while reporting no impact to Mistral's global infrastructure.
external_assessments.vigil_comparison_note: VIGIL treats the occurrence as a software-supply-chain package-provenance and release-integrity failure in ordinary-language governance terms, while retaining the Incident as unclassified under Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 because no current selectable class precisely encodes malicious package-distribution substitution.
